clinical_knowledge.topic: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

A suspected lung cancer requires tissue diagnosis, complete staging, pulmonary-function assessment, and multidisciplinary review; surgery is appropriate only when disease is resectable and the patient is an operative candidate.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with chronic cough and 3 cm lung mass in smoker, staging normal. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Benign granuloma without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Hemoptysis or new bone pain.
management_principles: Obtain tissue diagnosis, complete staging and physiologic assessment, then use multidisciplinary review to determine whether resection, systemic therapy, radiation, or combined treatment is appropriate
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
